title: Multi-User Security Analysis of ASCON
summary: The current ASCON security result does not directly extend to multiple users because a bad-event term scales with the user count; a separate multi-user bound remains open.

formal_statement.body: Develop a separate multi-user security analysis of ASCON that yields a security bound accounting for the first bad-event contribution $\frac{\mu(q_p+\sigma)}{2^\kappa}$, where $\mu$ is the number of users; the existing analysis does not directly extend to this setting because this contribution acquires the factor $\mu$.

scope.domain: Multi-user security bounds for ASCON authenticated encryption.
parameters: qₚ and σ — additive quantities in the first bad-event contribution
κ — denominator exponent in the first bad-event contribution
scope.unresolved_remainder: Develop a separate multi-user ASCON security analysis yielding a bound that accounts for the user-count factor in the first bad-event contribution.

progress.summary: The source observes that the first bad-event term gains a factor equal to the number of users, so the current ASCON result does not directly extend. It calls for a separate multi-user analysis.
citation_labels: Bishwajit Chakraborty et al., Exact Security Analysis of ASCON
